prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1063; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver. Reports a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Both vehicles drivable. Insured states the other driver crossed the center line while turning. Reported neck stiffness at the scene, declined EMS transport.

Entry 2: Recorded a recorded statement from the claimant. Claimant reports neck strain with pain rated moderate, worse when turning head. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says they have not yet decided whether to seek medical treatment. Advised claimant of the medical payments coverage and the process for submitting bills and records.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles received from the insured. Damage consistent with low-speed impact, bumper cover and front grille on the insured vehicle, rear quarter panel on the claimant vehicle. Scheduled appraisal at the local shop for the following business day.

Entry 4: Appraisal completed. Estimate reviewed against photos and the reported point of impact. Damage pattern supports the reported mechanism. Claimant has since visited an urgent care facility for neck strain and was prescribed a muscle relaxant and a referral to physical therapy. Requested the medical records and itemized bill with the claimant's signed authorization.

Entry 5: Received the urgent care records and itemized bill. Injury documented as cervical strain with limited range of motion. No prior neck complaints noted in the file. Liability accepted as clear based on the statement and physical evidence. Sent a written explanation of benefits and the next steps for the bodily injury evaluation to the claimant, who remains unrepresented. Diary set for follow-up with the physical therapy provider.
